::: {.why}
The checks you ran last night are not aesthetic; each violation corresponds to a specific portfolio of options with a guaranteed profit, and being able to name that portfolio is what makes the conditions memorable.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the static no-arbitrage conditions on an option surface and name the trade that each violation permits.
- Report which conditions your fitted surface violates and whether the cause is arbitrage or bad data.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Work out the trades: monotonicity in strike is a call spread with a negative price, convexity in strike is a butterfly with a negative price, and monotonicity of total variance in maturity is a calendar spread with a negative price. Write each as an explicit position, since that is how it is asked.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Audit your own surface: run all three checks across the whole chain and report the violations. In practice most will be stale quotes on illiquid strikes rather than real arbitrage, so also report the bid-ask spread at each violating point, which usually explains it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add the filter to your pipeline: a surface used for anything downstream must pass the three conditions after filtering, and points that fail are dropped with the reason recorded.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The three no-arbitrage checks implemented with the violating trade named for each, and an audit of your own surface with spreads reported.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your surface is not convex in strike at one point. What trade does that permit, and why is it probably not free money?
:::
